Transcript:
[00:00] Carlos: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Carlos from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with Aisha who is our se, and we wanted to run through a quick intro and discovery about Luminary's infra and see where partnership makes sense
[00:12] Nathan: thanks Carlos, yeah i'm Nathan, partnerships lead at Luminary, with Priya and Elliot from our side, excited to chat
[00:18] Aisha: hi all, quick agenda - partner program overview, technical compat, and go-to-market ops, is that good?
[00:25] Priya: yep that works, we want to understand commercials and timelines too
[00:30] Carlos: great, so at high level Redwood's inference platform supports hosted, dedicated and private deployments, we focus on consistent latency/cost across those modes - and partner integrations typically fall into co-sell + tech validation and sometimes an on-prem reseller model
[00:46] Elliot: quick clarifying q, when you say dedicated do you mean reserved capacity in your cloud or on our hardware?
[00:52] Aisha: good question, dedicated usually refers to reserved pools on Redwood-managed infra, but we also support private deployments - vpc or full on-prem - where the control plane can be customer-managed. there are differences re: sso, audit logs, kms etc
[01:10] Nathan: on Luminary side we sell rack units with 8x A100-class cards (we have our own naming), and we're onboarding a new 4u variant next quarter with nvlink 'ish, we call it L8-4u, um some customers ask for turnkey racks plus collocation
[01:28] Carlos: ok cool, do you expose IB / rdma to tenants? that's one of the things our runtime expects for multi-gpu and kv cache perf
[01:35] Elliot: yes we support ib with 100/200g options, and nvlink bridging on certain SKUs; there's some variability across regions though
[01:44] Aisha: perfect - for latency-sensitive workloads we look at kernel selection and nvlink topology; do you have a standard topo doc or is it bespoke per order?
[01:52] Elliot: there's a standard blueprint but customers can customize; we'll share a block diagram after the call
[02:05] Priya: on the business side, we are exploring channel partnerships - we can do referral fees, or a resale where Luminary bundles the infra and some managed services and Redwood provides the inference layer, how do you typically structure that?
[02:18] Carlos: we do a couple of models - referral/intro fees, co-sell with revenue share, and for strategic partners there's a reseller agreement. our partner team will propose program tiers; pricing differs if it's hosted vs dedicated vs private, and if there's an SLA or custom support included
[02:36] Nathan: what about benchmarks? customers often want to see per-token cost and p99 latency on common models, can you run things on your infra or do we run them on ours?
[02:46] Aisha: we can do both - Redwood hosted infra can run our standard benchmarks; for partner validation we usually run a joint benchmark on partner hardware to validate kernel/quantization behavior and networking - we have a spreadsheet with test cases, we'll share it
[02:58] Nathan: ok cool, that'd be helpful
[03:05] Priya: security is big for our enterprise prospects - SOC 2, ISO, audit logs, sso/saml, kms - what do you need from us?
[03:15] Carlos: we require standard security docs for marketplace and private deployments - we'll send our SOC2, compliance pack, and a security questionnaire; for private/on-prem we need details on network topologies, firewall rules, and key management (KMS/HSM) integration possibilities
[03:31] Elliot: we do provide KMS integration and can support bring-your-own-key for rack customers, and we have a basic audit log pipeline
[03:40] Aisha: one technical thing i want to flag - quantization and compilation paths. some partner GPUs have altered fp16 behavior or custom kernels; for our runtime we need to verify that models (especially 8k context transformers) run without large quality regressions when quantized to int8 or nf4, etc
[03:55] Elliot: yep we have customers running quantized models; we'll need to know which model families you validate - do you support llama-family, mosaic, and commercial ones?
[04:06] Carlos: we maintain a curated catalog of open and verified models; we also have guidance for custom model onboarding. SEs usually run a test corpus and we track regression alerts against reference prompts
[04:20] Nathan: timeline - if we wanted to get this integrated for Q4 co-sell push, what's realistic?
[04:26] Carlos: if we start tech validation now, run joint benchmarks and sign a basic partner agreement, Q4 is feasible. main risk is integration testing and any hardware-specific kernel work which could add 3-6 weeks
[04:38] Priya: commercial asks - do you have partner pricing? wholesale discounts?
[04:42] Carlos: we have partner pricing tiers; for resellers we provide committed capacity discounts, and for co-sell we do rev share. i'll put an initial outline in the follow-up email
[04:51] [05:00] (crosstalk, brief interruption)
[05:10] Aisha: couple of technical questions - network egress patterns, and how you handle prefix caching / KV cache across multi-tenant workloads? we sometimes see cache thrash if networking isn't consistent
[05:24] Elliot: our orchestration supports host-local caching, and we can configure vlan isolation per tenant; curious what caching patterns Redwood expects
[05:32] Aisha: we do a mix - automatic prefix caching and optional persistent KV cache for hot models. for dedicated we keep cache warm across instance lifetimes; for hosted we sandbox per-tenant. it helps if the partner infra offers predictable cold-start characteristics and good inter-node bandwidth
[05:50] Nathan: any compliance limitations for co-located racks in EU? some of our customers require data residency
[05:58] Carlos: we can do region pinning and private deployments to meet residency; we'd need to coordinate on data retention policies and logs access
[06:08] Priya: ok great. Elliot, can you share the architecture diagram after the call?
[06:12] Elliot: yes i'll get it to Nathan and Carlos by friday
[06:18] Nathan: a couple of potential gotchas we've seen - some partners have firmware/driver issues with newer kernel builds, do you run into that?
[06:25] Aisha: occasionally; part of the validation is a minimal supported driver matrix. if there's a custom vendor kernel we may need to build a shim or run a compatibility test suite
[06:36] Carlos: on the GTM side, we usually co-list partners in our marketplace if there's a validated integration; that includes joint marketing assets, a tech brief and a benchmark report. are you open to co-marketing?
[06:47] Priya: absolutely, that's a key incentive for us
[06:51] [10:00] (fast-forward, mid-call)
[10:05] Elliot: about telemetry - what's required for you to run regressions and monitor quality?
[10:10] Aisha: we typically ask for anonymized traces, token-level latencies, and output samples for eval prompt sets; for private deployments we can toggle retention settings - we prefer minimized PII and encrypted transport
[10:23] Nathan: on legal, we might need a partner addendum to the standard msa - anything special you require?
[10:29] Carlos: partner addendum is normal. we also have data processing addendums for EU customers. legal will share templates once we progress
[10:36] Priya: let's talk about a concrete pilot - could we do a 30-day pilot where Redwood runs inference on Luminary hardware in our lab and we run joint benchmarks?
[10:46] Aisha: yes that's the usual path. we can run a pilot with a small model set (say 7b/13b and one larger 70b if you support it) and run perf/cost comparisons and sample quality checks
[10:59] Elliot: we support up to 70b but need to check memory configs; we'll list recommended SKUs in the diagram
[11:10] Carlos: perfect - main deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet, topology diagram, and a follow-up technical deep-dive scheduled. we'll include contact for partner ops
[11:21] Nathan: commercial side - what's the minimum commitment for a reseller discount?
[11:26] Carlos: depends on region and capacity; typically a monthly committed vram or throughput commit. i'll include ranges in the outline
[11:35] [20:00] (closing segment)
[20:05] Aisha: any other technical blockers?
[20:09] Priya: no, just want to ensure timelines line up with our Q4 push
[20:12] Carlos: good. recap: Aisha shares benchmark file; Nathan/Elliot share topology; Carlos drafts partner email & pricing; legal exchange NDA and partner questionnaire. target follow-ups: Aisha's benchmarks by 8/25, Carlos email by 8/24, topology by 8/28, schedule deep-dive week of 8/31
[20:35] Nathan: sounds good, thanks everyone
[20:38] Priya: thanks, appreciate the time
[20:41] Carlos: thanks all - we'll follow up with notes and next steps. end call
